user_confirmed.material_scope: TA2/titanium research; existing optical-Ti models remain approximations
user_confirmed.research_priority: Study geometry and angular-domain performance jointly; include primary-structure manufacturability and feasibility of subsequent hierarchical structuring and coating control when selecting geometry families and bounds

not_yet_fixed.target_cone_axis: normal-centered working hypothesis, not a newly confirmed application specification

recommended_design_sequence_not_a_new_so: Define brightness/concentration metrics without prematurely locking a single cone half-angle
Bound geometry families using primary machining, secondary structuring access, and selective coating or filling feasibility
Screen geometric angular transport under common idealized emitter/reflector boundary conditions without requiring a real coating; retain throughput, source area, and projected-area normalization
Compare shortlisted geometries with fixed physical material and reference surface configurations using 3-20 um spectral-angular calculations
Calibrate representative designs with FEM and retained quality labels
Optimize constrained geometry parameters with a multi-fidelity surrogate and new-design validation
Test coating sensitivity on a small set of shortlisted geometries to check rank stability and geometry-coating interactions

coating_geometry_decoupling.meaning: A controlled staged study, not an assumption of physical independence or separable emissivity; a real reference coating is optional for ideal geometric screening, but optical boundary conditions and source distribution must be explicitly fixed

recommended_model_levels.surface_model: Fixed Lambertian bottom radiance and ideal specular reflecting walls; not an all-PEC thermal emitter
recommended_model_levels.scope: Angular redistribution and throughput under stated boundary conditions, not actual Ti emission or full-band wave validation

recommended_model_levels.surface_model: Same Ti optical model and specified surface state across geometries
recommended_model_levels.scope: Real-material geometry response without coating; small representative controls rather than mandatory full duplication

recommended_model_levels.surface_model: Fixed chosen coating/fill/secondary-surface treatment on shortlisted geometries
recommended_model_levels.scope: Estimate attainable spectral-angular performance and test ranking sensitivity

coating_geometry_decoupling.reference_coating_choice: Existing SiO2 floorfill is a possible reference, not a proven optimal 3-20 um absorber; final reference thickness is not selected by this update
coating_geometry_decoupling.diagnostic_option_not_a_physical_replace: Fast idealized bottom-emitter/reflector comparison may isolate angular transport; clearly label separately from physical Ti/SiO2 predictions

secondary_structuring: bottom and wall access for intended secondary feature location
secondary feature scale relative to wavelength
preservation of primary reflector surface and substrate thickness
coating_control: intended bottom versus wall versus conformal coverage
adhesion and stability up to 523 K
manufacturing_feasibility_in_geometry_se.numeric_bounds_status: To be grounded in available equipment and small fabrication trials; no unsupported hard dimension cutoffs added
manufacturing_feasibility_in_geometry_se.workflow: Compare optical merit and manufacturing feasibility together; retain interpretable baselines and realistic rounded geometries

recommended_reporting.temperature_weighting: Planck weighting within 3-20 um at specified T; maximum 523 K is not the entire operating range
recommended_reporting.polarization: unpolarized emissivity is the mean of matched s and p channels
angular_metrics: band cone-to-hemisphere power fraction as a function of cone half-angle
angular peak and width when well defined
recommended_reporting.cone_choice_status: comparison only; neither is imposed as a fixed target

limitations: A 523 K Planck-weighted result with fixed optical constants does not validate temperature-dependent materials or thermal stability
Existing 10.5 um normal-incidence WFT cases are calibration anchors, not broadband cone measurements
Existing v0 FEM training geometries all have bottom flat-to-flat width 15 um; width response is not learned from varying training widths
revision_note: Main band is 3-20 um. Clarified that ideal geometric screening does not require a physical reference coating, and user requires primary and subsequent composite/coating manufacturability to shape geometry choices from the start
operational_effect: No solver launch, termination, frozen manifest change, or resource-guard change in this objective update
